task_description: Write a method in Dafny to perform index wise multiplication of elements in the given two sequences.
specification_response:

    method SequenceWiseMultiplication(s1: seq<int>, s2: seq<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The length of the result sequence should be equal to the length of the input sequences
    - Each element in the result sequence should be the product of the corresponding elements in s1 and s2
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method ElementWiseMultiply(seq1: seq<int>, seq2: seq<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.

    - Both sequences should have the same length
    
Dafny specification:

Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The result sequence should have the same length as the input sequences
    - Each element in the result sequence should be the product of the corresponding elements in the input sequences
    
Dafny specification:
    ensures result != null

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method ElementWiseMultiply(seq1: seq<int>, seq2: seq<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires seq1 != null
    requires seq2 != null
    requires |seq1| == |seq2|
    ensures result != null
    ensures result.Length == seq1.Length
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < result.Length ==> result[i] == seq1[i] * seq2[i]
{
    result := new seq<int>(|seq1|);
    var i := 0;
    while i < seq1.Length
        invariant 0 <= i <= seq1.Length
        invariant result != null
        invariant result.Length == seq1.Length
        invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> result[j] == seq1[j] * seq2[j]
    {
        result := result[0..i] + [seq1[i] * seq2[i]] + result[i+1..];
        i := i + 1;
    }
}
```
